constants: Text: heavy wide grotesque sans, all caps, white fill, black stroke, soft black drop shadow (20 of 20)
Text block: two lines, top left, biggest line about 20 percent of frame height (20 of 20)
Arrow: white curved arrow with black outline from the text down to the bottom-left quadrant (20 of 20)
Ground: full-bleed stylised US state map with black state lines (20 of 20); no photo, no host
Hazard colours: magenta or pink snow bands, red severe zones, lime green or green rims; saturated against blue, purple or dark ground
Warning triangle: yellow with black exclamation mark, bottom-right (7 of 20, all popular)
Storm spiral graphic: white cloud spiral (4 of 20: n 5, 11, 13, 20)

host_treatment.note: No thumbnail shows a person. There is no lighting, cut-out, size or placement to measure. The brand is the map, the caps word and the arrow. A presenter rule cannot be tested on this channel.

text_rules.colours: white fill, black stroke, drop shadow; no coloured words
text_rules.highlight: none; no word coloured, boxed or enlarged beyond the stack
text_rules.content: reaction words (NO WAY 5, NOT GOOD 4, OH WOW 2, GET READY 3, HERE WE GO 2, THIS IS BIG 1); reaction plus subject (TONS OF SNOW! 1, HUGE SNOW 1, BIG SHIFT 1)
text_rules.title_repeat: 0 of 20 copy a title phrase; 1 paraphrase (n 16, GET READY for 'Nobody Is Ready')

popular_vs_latest.popular_1_10: magenta or pink snow band in 8 of 10 (n 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10); yellow warning triangle in 7 of 10; one spiral storm (n 5); views 1.4M to 8.7M
popular_vs_latest.latest_11_20: red as the main hazard colour in 8 of 10 (n 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19); yellow warning triangle in 0 of 10; three spiral storms (n 11, 13, 20); views 592k to 1.7M
popular_vs_latest.text: popular: NO WAY 4, OH WOW 2, one each of NOT GOOD, HUGE SNOW, TONS OF SNOW!, BIG SHIFT; latest: GET READY 3, NOT GOOD 3, HERE WE GO 2, THIS IS BIG 1, NO WAY 1
popular_vs_latest.data_flag: n 14 is labelled latest but has 1.7M views, which is above the popular list floor of 1.4M (n 8 to 10). The popular list may come from a different snapshot. Check meta.json before quoting popular rankings.

top3.shared: magenta snow zone on a blue or cyan ground; white two-to-three-word caps top-left with black stroke; white curved arrow to bottom-left; full-bleed US map; no face. n 2 and n 3 add the yellow warning triangle; n 1 has none.

transfer: Rule 1, two-word caps reaction, white with black stroke, two lines, top left. Evidence: n 1 NO WAY (8.7M), n 3 NO WAY (2.4M), n 6 NOT GOOD (1.5M); 16 of 20 use two words.
Rule 2, one bold white arrow with black outline from the text to the hazard. Evidence: all 20 have it; the top 3 (n 1, 2, 3) all do.
Rule 3, one saturated hazard colour that contrasts with the ground and fills the region. Evidence: magenta on blue or cyan for snow in n 1, 2, 3 (top 3); red on dark for severe in n 16, 17, 19.

Rule 4, yellow warning triangle bottom-right for winter threats. Evidence: 7 of 10 popular, 0 of 10 latest; n 2 (2.5M), n 3 (2.4M), n 4 (2.1M). Correlation only, test it on the next uploads before adopting.

Rule 5, text never copies the title; it adds a reaction plus one subject word (TONS OF SNOW!, HUGE SNOW, BIG SHIFT) or a call to act (GET READY). Evidence: 0 of 20 repeat the title; n 2 and n 4 are both in the top 4 by views.
weak: n 15 (592k, lowest view count in the set): heat-map gradient with no hard edge; the white arrow sits on yellow and the zone reads as temperature, not a storm.
n 17 (614k): blurred red blob with a dark core and no edge; the green rim reads as fair weather, so the hazard boundary is unclear.
n 8 (1.4M): lime-green zone on red-brown; green usually reads as calm, so the colour signal is mixed even though the view count is high.
